newsitem.title: USA: Lone Star Gas, Pipeline to fight examiner proposal.
newsitem.headline: Lone Star Gas, Pipeline to fight examiner proposal.

text.p: Lone Star Pipeline Co said on Tuesday that it and Lone Star Gas Co would likely suffer large financial losses if preliminary recommendations of hearing examiners related to rates were adopted by regulators.
Lone Star said it filed a case with the Railroad Commission of Texas last autumn looking to boost the average rate charged residential customers by about $0.90 per month.

But in a preliminary recommendation issued Monday, Lone Star said examiners proposed a 16 percent reduction in the profit margin allowed the company, which would reduce the average residential customer's bill by about $0.50 per month.
In addition, the examiners would impose severe financial penalties on the company's shareholders for the prices paid by Lone Star for customers' natural gas supply, Lone Star said.
In November Texas Utilities shareholders approved a takeover of ENSERCH Corp, including its Lone Star distribution and pipeline companies.
"This proposal is totally unjust and unreasonable and legally unsupportable," Lone Star Pipeline President Mike Hunter said, adding the company would protest the plan.
Hunter said the rate request was based on Lone Star's revenues and expenses during a recent 12-month study period.
"During the year studied, these businesses earned a before-tax income of approximately $39 million which was not sufficient to compensate us fairly for our $530 million investment," he said.

"Under the examiners' proposal, we would have incurred a loss of approximately $45 million during the year. Clearly, no company could stay in business for long being forced to suffer losses of this magnitude."
The company said this was the first increase it had sought for this rate in 14 years.
